questions: Should the replacement be applied only to exact string matches of the two-character sequence backslash-n, or to actual newline characters (line breaks) in the CSV data?
If the specified column does not exist, should the function raise an error, print a message and exit, print a message and return the unchanged DataFrame, or silently return the unchanged DataFrame?

Should the replacement be applied to all columns or only the specified column? The clarification says 'in the specified column', but the original prompt also said 'after stripping whitespace' which is now removed; is the column restriction still intended?
If the file does not exist, should the function raise an exception, print a message and exit, print a message and return an empty DataFrame, or do something else?
Should the replacement be case-sensitive? (e.g., should '\N' or '\n' in different cases be replaced?)
Should the replacement use regex=True (allowing special regex characters in the pattern) or exact string replacement?
Should the function modify the DataFrame in-place or return a new DataFrame?
If the column contains NaN or other non-string values, should the replacement still be attempted, or should those values be left unchanged?
